chosen.premise: While foraging, female Nidoran use whiskers to read the wind and stay downwind of predators.
chosen.hook: Nidoran♀ can use its whiskers to hide from predators.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate whiskers sampling wind arrows as Nidoran♀ moves to the downwind side.
chosen.note: A highly specific, unusual survival mechanic exclusive to the female entry, with a clear wind-direction animation. The hook should say it detects wind and stays downwind, not simply that it hides.

candidates.premise: Female Nidoran has a smaller, more rounded horn tip than the male, but it still secretes venom.
candidates.hook: Her horn is smaller and rounder—but still poisonous.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen the female and male horn descriptions, then overlay a venom warning.
candidates.note: A precise female-versus-male distinction with a useful contradiction, though the comparison requires showing another Pokémon and is less behaviorally distinctive.

candidates.premise: Nidoran♀ avoids fighting, yet its venom can kill from a single drop or tiny scratch.
candidates.hook: This Pokémon hates fighting—but its poison can still kill you.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a calm Nidoran♀ beside escalating text: tiny scratch, one drop, fatal.
candidates.note: Strong contradiction backed by multiple Pokédex entries, though the general docile-versus-dangerous setup could fit several Poison Pokémon.

candidates.premise: Nidoran♀ reaches Nidorina at level 16, then needs a Moon Stone to become Nidoqueen.
candidates.hook: Nidoran♀ evolves twice—but the second evolution needs a Moon Stone.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a level-16 progress bar becoming Nidorina, then a Moon Stone unlocking Nidoqueen.
candidates.note: Concrete and highly visual, but evolution requirements are familiar Pokémon information and the cited methods rely on trusted secondary data.

candidates.premise: Nidoran♀'s small body is protected by venomous barbs and a poison-secreting horn.
candidates.hook: Its entire defense system is built into tiny spikes.
candidates.visualIdea: Highlight the horn and barbs on Nidoran♀, then label them as its protection.
candidates.note: Well supported and easy to illustrate, but it is a broad anatomy profile rather than one sharply surprising claim.

candidates.premise: Nidoran♀ is docile until threatened, when it answers with poison spikes and a horrible toxin.
candidates.hook: Threaten this gentle Pokémon, and its defense gets terrifying.
candidates.visualIdea: Switch from a peaceful Nidoran♀ to animated spikes and toxin warning graphics.
candidates.note: The behavioral switch is compelling, but it overlaps heavily with the docile-but-deadly angle and uses dramatic wording not fully established by the evidence.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required. Keep the episode focused on the unusual mechanic that female Nidoran reads wind direction with its whiskers and stays downwind of predators; avoid expanding it into a generic poison or evolution profile.
